meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

приготовить.gloss: to prepare, to cook, to make

meanings.en: to cook, to make (food), to prepare

examples.text: Я торт приготовила. Ты любишь сладкое?
examples.trans: I made a cake. Do you have a sweet tooth?

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'egg' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: It is time to add the eggs.

examples.text: Макс, быстрее! Уже пора добавлять яйца.
examples.trans: Max, faster! It is time to add the eggs.

examples.text: Берём свежие яйца и разогреваем сковороду.
examples.trans: We take fresh eggs and heat the frying pan.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem '-парижски').

examples.text: Это слово «по-парижски» часто звучит в разговоре.
examples.trans: This word 'Parisian-style' is often heard in conversation.
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

examples.text: Слушай, Нина, это же тот самый ресторан!
examples.trans: Listen, Nina, this is that very restaurant!

examples.text: Мы рады видеть вас в нашем ресторане.
examples.trans: We are glad to see you in our restaurant.
They called from the Italian restaurant.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

снять.gloss: to film, to photograph; to take off; to rent

meanings.en: to film, to take a photo/video of

examples.text: Я сняла пьяного соседа на телефон.
examples.trans: I filmed a drunk neighbour on my phone.
He took off his coat by the door.

examples.text: Я сняла пьяного соседа на телефон. И сразу все мне помогают!
examples.trans: I filmed a drunk neighbour on my phone. And right away everyone helps me!

meanings.note: кого + instrumental: назвать меня плохим словом

examples.trans: You called me a bad word.
What will you name your son?

examples.text: Ты назвал меня плохим словом. Меня, начальника!
examples.trans: You called me a bad word. Me, your boss!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'понсор'). Common masculine noun meaning 'sponsor, backer' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Мы не можем продолжать кампанию без спонсоров.
examples.trans: We cannot continue the campaign without sponsors.

examples.text: Мы не можем продолжать кампанию без спонсоров. Нам даже плакаты напечатать не на что.
examples.trans: We cannot continue the campaign without sponsors. We don't even have money to print posters.

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

meanings.note: pointing at something a little way off
вон отсюда! = get out of here!

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели. Я решу все ваши проблемы.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.

meanings.note: как вы знаете = as you know

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: много дел = a lot to do

examples.trans: I have a lot to do.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'втра').

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
present есть; у меня есть = I have

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'full house' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Это слово «аншлаг» часто звучит в разговоре.
examples.trans: This word 'full house' is often heard in conversation.

meanings.note: Core Russian part meaning 'even' in everyday speech.
Core Russian name meaning 'Bianca' in everyday speech.

Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'ехать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to arrive (by vehicle)', paired with 'приезжать'.

examples.trans: Which car did you come in?

examples.text: Вика, ты на какой машине сегодня приехала?
examples.trans: Vika, which car did you come in today?
Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.note: 'что я за мэр такой' = what kind of mayor am I

examples.text: Паша, я больше не хочу о ней слышать. Понял?
examples.trans: Pasha, I don't want to hear about her again. Understood?

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)

meanings.note: in threats: ты ещё увидишь = you'll see

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: agrees in gender and case with the noun

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'trump card' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: У меня есть еще один козырь.
examples.trans: I have another ace up my sleeve.

examples.text: Это слово «козырь» часто звучит в разговоре.
examples.trans: This word 'trump card' is often heard in conversation.

examples.text: Макс решил забронировать столик на вечер.
examples.trans: Max decided to reserve a table for the evening.

examples.text: Алло, ресторан, я хочу забронировать столик.
examples.trans: Hello, restaurant, I want to reserve a table.
Book a table for Prokhor Mikhailov.

examples.text: Они заняли свободный столик у окна.
examples.trans: They took a free table near the window.
Would you like to sit at an available table?
To a guest at the next table.
We could open a salon for you.

examples.text: Для вас можно открыть салон красоты.
examples.trans: We could open a beauty salon for you.

meanings.note: Core Russian name meaning 'Prokhor' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Book a table for Prokhor Mikhailov.

examples.text: Вика, Паша! Как я рад. Проходите, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Vika, Pasha! I'm so glad. Come in, please.

meanings.note: Core Russian name meaning 'Mikhailova' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Book a table for Prokhor Mikhailov.

examples.text: Так, операцию продолжаем. Михаил Михайлович, помогайте Лаврову.
examples.trans: Right, the operation goes on. Mikhail Mikhailovich, give Lavrov your help.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'oligarch' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The oligarch will dine with us?

examples.text: Это слово «олигарх» часто звучит в разговоре.
examples.trans: This word 'oligarch' is often heard in conversation.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'жинать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to dine'.

examples.trans: The oligarch will dine with us?

examples.text: Это слово «ужинать» часто звучит в разговоре.
examples.trans: This word 'to dine' is often heard in conversation.

meanings.note: accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)

meanings.en: other forms: его (gen/acc), ему (dat), им (instr), нём (prep)

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Я точно не помню его адрес.
examples.trans: I don't remember his exact address.

examples.text: Точно, полиция была! А что с машиной?
examples.trans: That's right, the police were there! And what about the car?

examples.text: Решается ваш вопрос, Клавдия Викторовна! Вы не видите, у меня встреча?
examples.trans: Your question is being sorted out, Klavdia Viktorovna! Can't you see I have a meeting?
